reason: Checked against the source. update_mover's only reference is JSR update_mover in update_movers_loop, right after LDY movers_to_update,X : STY mover_to_update, so Y = mover_to_update on entry, and the new prologue never changes Y (animate_explosion_or_skeleton and um0db5_update see the same Y). Arithmetic: CMP #&F5 vs right_low gives C=0 exactly when right_low+&0A carries; SBC then gives x_high-(right_high+c), so BCC/BNE/equal match the original's CPX &C5 BCC/BNE, and on equal C=1 so ADC #&09 = right_low+&0A, then CMP movers_x_low,Y matches CMP mover_x_low. right_high <= &1D, so no wrap; removed movers (x_high &FF) leave in both. Dropped stores &F8 (mover_x_low/end_of_run_offset), &F9 (mover_y/column_length_in_bytes/pixel), &C5 (result/source_address): on the animate path plot_mover writes &F8/&C5 before it reads them, and walk_column, check_if_mover_is_on_screen and plot_mover_sprite never read &F9 (the only mover_y readers are move_mover_set_43fa, cmxy_add_height, check_for_collision_with_mover and search_for_target_with_offset, which come after a get_mover_Y_x_and_y on the update path). update_enemy_helicopter runs unconditionally after the loop and starts check_if_mover_can_be_updated -> check_for_player_collision_with_mover_Y -> get_mover_Y_x_and_y, so all three hold the same values at the end of the pass, before render_pass's save_game_zp/restore_game_zp (render_zp saves and restores &F8/&F9). None of the IRQ code uses them. Not protected (grind_config PROTECT lists only irq1_handler, not_vsync_2ed0 and wait_for_vsync_2242). No generated source and no table changed; the tables are in main RAM &13xx below &3000, so ACCCON X and ROMSEL do not matter. Bytes: old 25, new 22, plus 3 bytes of EQUB padding after the JMP in non-gameplay builds, so nothing after it moves. Gameplay builds drop the padding (3 bytes smaller), as the neighbouring paddings already do (decision 43). The front end, game over and completion screen never run update_mover, and the helicopter path is covered by the helicopter's own re-read. Cycles: the on-screen path (x_high < limit) goes from 57 to 15 and the leave-by-high path from 52 to 17, so the claimed ~34 a call average is plausible.
